      "content": "# Change record: status_counts report\n\n## What changed\n\n`logreports/reports/status_counts.py` now implements `summarize(records)`. It starts from `{'2xx': 0, '3xx': 0, '4xx': 0, '5xx': 0}`. For each record it increments the key `f\"{status // 100}xx\"` if that key is in the dict. The result always has all four keys, so classes with no records are `0`. Empty input gives all zeros.\n\nThe function does not mutate its input. Its result is a plain dict of integers, so it is JSON-serializable.\n\n## Why it matters\n\nThe `status_counts` module was a stub. `python3 -m logreports input.jsonl --report status_counts` now prints the counts as JSON with sorted keys. The CLI imports the module and calls `summarize(records)`, so no CLI change was needed.\n\n## Files\n\n- `logreports/reports/status_counts.py`: the implementation.\n- `tests/test_status_counts.py`: unittest cases for empty input, mixed input, unseen classes at zero, the boundaries 200, 299, 300, 399, 400, 499, 500 and 599, counts across services, non-mutation, JSON serializability with four keys, and the CLI with populated and empty files.\n- `docs/reports/status_counts.md`: output shape, class mapping, zero and empty behavior, and CLI usage.\n\n`logreports/core.py` and `logreports/__main__.py` are unchanged.\n\n## Behavior note\n\nA status outside 2xx to 5xx would be ignored, not counted. The loader accepts only integer statuses in 200..599, so this does not occur through the CLI.\n\n## How to verify\n\n```\npython3 -B -m unittest discover -s tests\npython3 -m logreports input.jsonl --report status_counts\n```\n\nThe controller's `test` and `build` checks and the independent review decide acceptance. This record does not.\n"
